sections.heading: Signs You Need a New One, and Signs You Don't
body: Most water heater trouble comes down to a short list of causes. Some are small parts, and some mean the tank is done. Here is how to tell them apart.

items.title: Water at the base of the tank
items.text: Water coming from the bottom usually means the tank itself has failed, and a leaking tank can't be patched. A drip from a pipe fitting above it is a different, smaller repair.

items.title: No hot water at all
items.text: On an electric heater this is often a heating element or a thermostat. On a gas heater it can be the pilot or the burner. These are repairs, and the tank goes on working.

items.title: Lukewarm water, or it runs out fast
items.text: Sediment piles up on the bottom of an older tank, and an element can wear down. Sometimes it's a repair. Sometimes it's the tank telling you it's near the end.

items.title: Rust-colored hot water
items.text: Rust in the hot water, or rust at the tank, points to corrosion inside. That doesn't reverse, and it's usually a sign to replace.

items.title: Rumbling or popping
items.text: That's sediment cooking on the bottom of the tank. It wears the tank out faster, and an older tank making those sounds is worth a look.

sections.heading: Gas, Electric or Propane
body: We repair and replace natural gas, electric and propane water heaters. Tell us which one you have when you call.
Not sure? Look for a gas line running to the unit, a thick electrical cable, or a propane tank outside the house. If you still can't tell, describe what you see and we'll work it out on the phone.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace?
body: Here's a rule you can check yourself. If the tank is sound and a part has failed, repair it. A new element or thermostat costs far less than a new water heater.
If the tank is leaking, rusting through, or old and failing in several ways, that's when to replace it. Money spent on a dying tank is often better put toward a new one.
We tell you which side of that line you're on, including when the answer is to repair.

sections.heading: What Happens When You Call About a Clogged Drain

image.alt: Bathroom sink and faucet in a Wichita home

body: Tell us which drain is giving you trouble and what it's doing: slow, gurgling, standing water, a smell. We ask whether it's one sink, one toilet or the whole house.
Then a technician comes out, finds the clog and clears it. We say what we found, so you know whether it was a one-time clog or a sign of something bigger.
If you've already tried a chemical drain cleaner, tell us. It can sit in the pipe, and whoever opens it up should know.

sections.heading: Where the Clog Is Tells You What It Is
body: Where the problem shows up says a lot about where it is. Here's how to read it.

items.title: One sink or tub is slow
items.text: Usually hair, soap or grease in the trap or the branch pipe behind that one fixture. It's the easiest clog to clear.

items.title: A toilet that keeps stopping up
items.text: Often something that shouldn't have been flushed, and sometimes a problem in the line past the toilet. If it keeps coming back, we look past the bowl.

items.title: Several fixtures slow at once
items.text: When the shower, sink and washer all drain slowly, the clog is likely in the main line that they all share.

items.title: Gurgling or a sewer smell
items.text: Gurgling means air is fighting through a partial clog. A smell means the water isn't moving the way it should. Call before it becomes a backup.

items.title: Water coming up in the floor drain
items.text: That's a backup in the main line. Stop using water in the house and call.

sections.quote: I have had several toilet issues mostly due to my young kids. It's frustrating how well toys and hair clips plug it up. I called Brand Plumbing. They were on time, professional, and a joy to work with.

sections.heading: Kitchen, Laundry and Bathroom Drains
body: Each room has its own usual suspect, and knowing it helps us find the problem faster when you call.

items.title: Kitchen sink
items.text: Grease and food waste collect past the trap and harden. A jammed garbage disposal is a separate repair, and we do same-day repairs on disposals, so tell us which one you have.

items.title: Laundry
items.text: Lint and soap build up in the standpipe and the line behind the washer. If the washer drain overflows during a load, stop the machine and call.

items.title: Bathroom
items.text: Hair and soap in the tub or shower, and paper or wipes in the toilet line. A hair catcher on the tub drain prevents most of it.

sections.heading: When It's More Than a Clog
body: Roots, a cracked section or a sag in the line can bring a clog back again and again. When a snake keeps finding the same trouble, the line itself is the problem.
We repair sewage and drain lines, and we replace water and sewer systems when repair isn't enough. We'll tell you plainly which one you're looking at.

sections.heading: Keeping Drains Clear
body: A few habits keep most drains running. Use a hair catcher in the shower, keep grease out of the kitchen sink, and flush only toilet paper.
A drain that slows down a little more each month is asking for attention. Calling early is almost always a smaller job than calling after it backs up.

items.q: Can you clear a clogged toilet?
items.a: Yes. We repair toilets and clear the drains behind them. Tell us what happened and whether it's the only toilet in the house that's stopped up.

items.q: Do you handle sewer line problems?
items.a: Yes. We repair sewage and drain lines and replace sewer systems. A technician looks at the problem first and tells you what it is.

items.q: Do you clear drains in commercial buildings?
items.a: We work on offices and rental properties as well as homes. Tell us what kind of building it is when you call.

items.q: What should I do before you come?
items.a: Stop using the drain, and if water is coming up anywhere, stop using water in the house. Tell us which fixtures are affected.
We won't guess at a number here, since it depends on where the clog is. Call and describe what's happening, and we'll tell you what the work involves.

why: Every page on your current site carries the same headline: “Brand Plumbing, Inc. Wichita, KS.” No page is built for a water heater or a drain. Someone with a cold shower on a weekday morning searches “water heater replacement Wichita KS” and finds nothing made for it.

Your Google reviews already say what you do well. Kathy B.: “They were so very responsive and able to replace it same day!” Teresa F.: “they were here Friday morning.” Today those words sit on Google, not on your site, and your phone number isn't a tap-to-call link on any page.

So the demo tells one story everywhere: call on a weekday, hear when we can come, and get hot water back. It opens with plumber in Wichita, KS, and gives water heater replacement and drain cleaning a page each. You list phone and email only, so the contact page leads with both.
